ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic sanctions screening of all directors, shareholders, and individuals with significant control. Screening is required under FINTRAC guidelines, the Special Economic Measures Act (SC 1992, c 17), and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (SC 2011, c 24). Lists screened include FINTRAC sanctions lists, OSFI-identified entities, the Canadian sanctions consolidated list, US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, and the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for PEPs, their family members, close associates, and high-risk jurisdictions; all screening results must be documented and retained in the AML/CFT compliance file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada Online Filing Centre for federal corporations; Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online portal for Quebec provincial corporations and extra-provincial registration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporations carrying on business in Quebec must comply with the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11). The legal name must have a French version, and the French version must be used with equal prominence in contracts, advertisements, and invoices. For non-Latin scripts, a transliteration into the Latin alphabet or French phonetic form is required; non-Latin characters are not accepted in the official corporate name. Federal corporations may use an English-only, French-only, or bilingual name, but extra-provincial registration in Quebec will require a French-language name variant.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Federal: A rejected proposed name may be appealed to the Director under the Canada Business Corporations Act by filing a written request for review within 30 days of the rejection, setting out the grounds; the Director reconsiders once, and a further challenge may be brought by way of judicial review before the Federal Court. Quebec: A refusal by the Registraire des entreprises may be contested by filing a reconsideration request with the Registraire within 30 days of the refusal notice under s 27 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; if the refusal is maintained, an appeal may be brought before the Court of Quebec or the Superior Court of Quebec depending on the nature and amount in issue. A modified NUANS report with a new distinctive element may also cure a rejection based on lack of distinctiveness.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional. The registered office of a Quebec or federal corporation must be a physical location within Quebec where books, records, and minute books are kept and where legal process may be served. A virtual office provided by a licensed corporate service agent can qualify if it comprises a genuine physical address, manned reception, and mail acceptance capacity; a non-physical PO Box, mail-forwarding-only arrangement, or purely remote address does not satisfy statutory requirements. For a digital health and fitness app business without a physical storefront, this type of registered-agent virtual office is commonly accepted by the Registraire des entreprises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate for a software-only activity. Unannounced on-site inspection of the registered office is estimated at under 5% annual probability during the first year; the risk increases to 10-15% once payroll, GST/QST, or corporate tax accounts are active, as CRA and Revenu Québec may perform compliance visits or audits at the registered office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec (RQ); portal: CRA My Business Account and Revenu Québec's CléNumérique / Mon Dossier d'entreprise
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident and resident corporations must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) via CRA Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or online through the Business Registration Online (BRO) service; Quebec-based corporations must additionally register with Revenu Québec via Form LM-1-V (Registration of an Enterprise) to obtain a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and provincial tax accounts (e.g., QST, source deductions, health services fund). For Federal/Provincial Business Corporation, articles of incorporation or registration with Corporations Canada or the Quebec Registraire des entreprises prior to tax registration; the BN and NEQ are linked through the integrated business registration workflow; foreign entities appoint a provincial agent for service if no physical Quebec presence, and each separate business activity requires a separate BN program account number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Canada; Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) status elections under ITA 125(7) and associated definitions apply; Quebec adopts federal taxable income as base with provincial adjustments; available elections include filing a joint election for deemed disposition of eligible capital property (ITA 14) and Form T2 Schedule 89 for eligible capital property transitional amounts; hybrid mismatch rules under ITA 18.5 and subsection 18.6 restrict deduction of payments subject to hybrid mismatch arrangements consistent with BEPS Action 2; Quebec's Taxation Act mirrors hybrid mismatch provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies for GST/HST (zero-rating exceptions for small suppliers); Quebec QST registration threshold is CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies in Canada unless the corporation is a 'large business' (threshold applies individually); once exceeded, mandatory registration effective on the transaction that breaches the threshold; non-resident digital suppliers may be required to register for simplified GST/HST and QST regardless of threshold if engaged in enumerated digital services and supplies to Quebec residents.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No universal B2B e-invoicing clearance mandate at federal level; CRA accepts electronic invoices if records are accessible in Canada; Quebec has a phased mandatory B2B e-invoicing (and B2C e-reporting) regime under Revenu Québec implemented from January 1, 2026 for enterprises with annual turnover exceeding CAD 50 million; PDF/A-3 format with embedded structured XML (Factur-X, ZUGFeRD or Universal Business Language) is required for Quebec e-invoices; no national digital stamping requirement; Pan-Canadian interoperability initiatives under the Council of the Federation may evolve.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods exported from Canada (ITA Schedule VI, Part V) and to certain digital services supplied to non-residents who are not registered for GST/HST and where the supply is not for use in Canada; remote digital services supplied to a consumer ordinarily resident in a participating province may be subject to HST; zero-rating of a cross-border service generally requires documentation demonstrating the recipient is a non-resident and the service is consumed entirely outside Canada; Quebec QST zero-rating mirrors the GST/HST scheme under the Quebec Taxation Act and regulations.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Invoice (CCI) or commercial invoice
Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency — G13/Canada Export Reporting)
Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
Proof of shipment (rail/air/sea waybill or courier manifest)
Evidence of foreign destination (delivery confirmation or customs entry at destination)
Foreign exchange wiring confirmation (equivalent to Inward Remittance Certificate) showing crediting of foreign currency to a Canadian bank account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the Excise Tax Act, a false or misleading statement for zero-rating can result in penalties of the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the net tax overstated; Knowingly making a false statement is subject to penalty of 50% of the net tax amount; CRA/QFC may assess additional GST/HST, QST, interest, and administrative penalties for failure to substantiate export zero-rating; criminal prosecution under the Tax Rebate and Calculation of Interest Rules and the Criminal Code may apply for fraudulent refund claims; the taxpayer bears the burden of proof, and clawback periods extend to four years from the date of assessment (or indefinitely in case of misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness or wilful default); exporter records must be retained for six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility. The Canadian dollar is freely floating; there are no exchange control laws or prior-approval requirements for capital inflows, outflows, profit remittances, dividends, interest, or royalties. Cross-border transfers are subject only to general AML/KYC documentation, FINTRAC reporting thresholds (e.g., CAD 10,000 or equivalent), and tax withholding obligations under the Income Tax Act and applicable tax treaties. Non-resident shareholders may freely repatriate lawful profits subject to procedural tax compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory requirement to surrender, convert, repatriate, or hold export proceeds in domestic currency. Exporters may retain foreign currency balances in domestic or foreign bank accounts. Administrative reporting to Statistics Canada for balance-of-payments purposes may apply, but there is no mandatory conversion ratio or repatriation timeline.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low for purely offshore EMIs without Canadian registration. Offshore digital banks and EMIs are not directly authorized to provide banking services without being recognized as either a Canadian federal/provincial chartered bank, a licensed foreign bank branch, or a registered money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Additionally, the Retail Payment Activities Act (and related Bank of Canada oversight) requires payment service providers to register. A cross-border EMI may become viable through a partnership with a Canadian Schedule I bank or through establishing an MSB in Canada, but standalone direct account-opening as a bank is legally constrained.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandated under Canadian federal AML rules. Canadian banks generally permit corporate onboarding with notarized or certified identification of directors and authorized signatories plus the full corporate KYC package. Remote video verification is increasingly accepted by Tier-1 banks for low-risk non-listed operating companies. However, banks retain discretion to require an in-person interview, board resolution, or registered office inspection, particularly when non-resident ownership, complex treasury flows, or unusual funding sources are present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) with opaque personal or corporate ownership chains
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extracts (federal or Quebec registraire des entreprises), UBO disclosure forms, personal government-issued ID, proof of residential address, notarized corporate resolutions, and apostilled/legalized documents from the home jurisdiction where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of initial capital derived from accumulated offshore digital app revenue (Apple/Google payments) that lacks a clear audit trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Historical financial statements, platform payout reports from Apple App Store Connect and Google Play Console, bank statements of the depositing entity, income tax filings, transfer-pricing documentation, and a written source-of-funds explanation with transactional traceability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or counterparty appearing on sanctions, PEP, or high-risk jurisdiction lists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and PEP screening clearance reports (OSFI/DFATD), commercial rationale letters, certificates of good standing, independent background checks, and legal opinions confirming no controlled or sanctioned party involvement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of physical substance or absence of a genuine place of business in Quebec/Canada
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office lease or sublease agreements, payroll records for local employees or outsourced service providers, Quebec business registration certificate, corporate insurance policies, and a detailed business plan showing real economic activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected large cross-border wires above reporting thresholds from or to diverse jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cash-flow forecast, underlying trade/service contracts for the health-fitness app platform, software licensing agreements, supplier invoices, investor funding agreements, and proactive FINTRAC-compliant transaction monitoring procedures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity or shareholder-loan funding from non-resident shareholders is wired via SWIFT MT103 to the Canadian corporation's designated account at a Tier-1 bank. The wire must reference the purpose as 'Share Capital Subscription' or 'Shareholder Loan/Direct Investment', the beneficiary corporate name, and the corporate registration number. Settlement occurs through Lynx (Canada's high-value clearing system) for CAD, or via USD clearing procedures for USD. No exchange-control approval is required; however, if the inbound investment triggers Investment Canada Act review thresholds, an investor notification or application may be necessary. Standard bank compliance supports the transfer with the incorporation certificate, constitutional documents, shareholder register, board resolutions, and source-of-funds evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade and service settlements may be executed through SWIFT MT103/MT202 for bank wire transfers, CAD clearings via Lynx, and retail payments via ACSS (Automated Clearing Settlement System). For letter of credit transactions, a commercial LC is opened through a Canadian chartered bank with an advising bank abroad, with documentary compliance required. Foreign currency payments are settled through correspondent banking networks. All disbursements must be supported by commercial contracts, invoices, and board-approved treasury policies to satisfy AML and corporate law documentation standards.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (CAD vs. foreign currencies)
Vanilla currency options (FX options for hedging commercial exposures)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Return (Déclaration annuelle) under the Quebec Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than June 15 of each year; or within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation depending on REQ-assigned annual return date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 15 per day up to CAD 750; after 30 days, REQ may initiate dissolution of the corporation; directors may be personally liable for continued default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (applicable if federally incorporated)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation date; must be filed within 60 days after the anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for one year may lead to administrative dissolution; late filing may result in penalties and loss of corporate status

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal and Quebec Corporate Income Tax Return (T2 / CO-17)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end for Canadian-controlled private corporations; within 3 months for other corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeated failure attracts higher penalties; directors may be liable for unremitted amounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements presented to shareholders at the annual meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; retained in the corporate minute book; available to REQ or CRA upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 months after the previous annual meeting; first annual meeting within 18 months after incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be in default under the Quebec Business Corporations Act; court may compel the holding of a meeting or production of financial statements; administrative penalties apply

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Private corporations are generally exempt from mandatory independent audit under the Quebec Business Corporations Act unless shareholders pass a resolution requiring an audit; mandatory audit applies to public corporations, reporting issuers, or corporations exceeding CAD 5 million in gross revenue and CAD 10 million in total assets (or other regulatory thresholds); CRA may demand audited financial statements under the Income Tax Act
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Canada for public enterprises; private enterprises may elect IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under the CPA Canada Handbook

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec requires a register of individuals with significant control under the Quebec Business Corporations Act; any individual or entity holding 25% or more of voting shares or with significant influence must be recorded; changes must be noted within 15 days; an annual confirmation of directors and registered office is filed with REQ; no standalone public UBO annual filing is required unless changes occur or REQ requests disclosure; federally incorporated corporations must comply with federal transparency requirements on a continuing basis
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 300-1,200 USD per year for registered office services in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 2,000-6,500 USD per year for a small private corporation statutory review or audit engagement in Quebec

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined (federal 15% general corporate rate + Quebec provincial 11.5% general corporate rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified Canadian-controlled private corporations benefit from the federal small business deduction on active business income up to CAD 500,000 (federal 9%); Quebec provincial small business rate on the same threshold is reduced to 3.6%. Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax credits provide a federal non-refundable credit of 15% and a refundable credit of 35% for eligible CCPCs; Quebec also grants an additional R&D tax credit around 14% and specific interactive digital media and IT validation credits for health-tech app development.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return – filed through the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) E-file portal using certified tax software or EFILE/Internet
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is six months after the corporation’s fiscal year-end; the balance of tax payable is due no later than two months after year-end (three months for eligible Canadian-controlled private corporations to the extent of its small business deduction).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from digital health and fitness app subscriptions, in-app purchases, biometric telemetry analytics licenses, and advertising income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Canadian-source business income attributable to PEs in Canada; for remote digital services into Canada without a PE, identify the income as foreign source and claim application of OECD nexus principles or withholding tax exemptions where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For SaaS or digital subscription products, include capitalized development costs and deferred cloud-hosting costs; no physical inventory generally.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident affiliates supplying software content, ensure the transfer-pricing adjustment is applied and reflected in inventory valuation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 340 – Depreciation of eligible capital property / Class 50 computing hardware
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital cost allowance (CCA) on servers, development equipment, and licensed biometric sensors. Assets used for zero-emission app infrastructure may qualify for accelerated CCA under Class 43.1.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the computing assets are owned by a foreign capital corporation and leased to the Canadian entity, lease rental deductions are arm’s-length and supported by Form T106 information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute net business income after adjusting for CCA, SR&ED claimed amounts, charitable donations, and any non-capital loss carrybacks.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations with a PE in Quebec report taxable income generally the same as resident corporations; deduct treaty and domestic permanent-establishment rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claimable SR&ED investment tax credits and Quebec R&D credits are entered on the T2, with supporting schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The federal Part XIII tax credit for non-resident shareholders is not deductible; this line only applies to the Canadian legal entity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty is 5% of the amount of tax unpaid when the return was due, plus 1% of unpaid tax per full month late, to a maximum 12 months. Repeated failure to file may trigger a separate penalty of 10% of the unpaid tax. Interest accrues daily on overdue amounts at the prescribed rate. Quebec imposes a parallel penalty on late filing of the CO-17 and late tax payment (additional 0.5-5% + interest).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return – Revenu Québec’s online portal (Clir) for taxpayers with a Quebec establishment
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Must be filed by the same six-month post-year-end deadline as the federal T2; the Quebec final balance for instalment remittances is due within the same two-month (or three-month eligible) window.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Replicate the federal reported computation for income from carrying on business in Quebec, after Quebec-specific adjustments for the Research and Development tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Quebec must compute the Quebec allocation percentage (including sales, payroll, and paid-up capital attribution for the province).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reflect federal taxable income adjusted for Quebec-only additions (e.g., certain interest penalties not deductible, Quebec political contributions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty relief cannot override the Quebec PE allocation; conservative allocation with documentary support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec health-services contribution calculated on the payroll of the establishment if over the CAD 200,000 annual payroll threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident employer with employees seconded to Quebec, the provincial payroll allocation may create a physical establishment exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec imposes a 5% penalty plus 1% per month on the unpaid amount for up to 18 months, plus daily late-filing fees. Directors are personally liable for unpaid deductibles, QST, and wage deductions when the corporation declares bankruptcy. Failure to register for the QST (Quebec GST equivalent) attracts penalties of CAD 250 plus reinstatement fees.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation (including a Quebec federal or provincial corporation) to a non-resident shareholder. This rate is a flat gross-basis withholding tax; the rate may be reduced under an applicable tax treaty (e.g., Canada-US treaty: 5% if the recipient is a company that owns 10% or more of voting shares; otherwise 15%; most treaties allow 15% portfolio dividend/5% substantive holding).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty-reduced dividend withholding tax, the non-resident shareholder must provide a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by its home tax authority to the Canadian resident paying corporation (or to the recognized withholding agent) before the payment date. The shareholder must complete and file CRA Form NR301 – Treaty-Based Return, declaring eligibility for treaty benefits (on an annual basis for each year in which relief is claimed). The Canadian payer must retain the form and evidence of residence in its books and respond to CRA cross-reference audits. For Quebec-relevant payments, a quebec counterpart (RL-1027) is not required; the federal NR301 process controls withholding at the Saskatchewan? Actually the provincial top-up? Revenu Québec generally follows the federal treaty positions, but the payer must also confirm no Quebec-specific additional levy applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII withholding tax on royalties for patents, software, and biometric IP is 25%; on interest it is also 25% unless the payee deals at arm’s length and is entitled to the exemption under paragraph 212(1)(b) for arm’s length interest paid by a non-resident-owned investment corporation, or under certain treaty protocols. Canada’s typical treaty-reduced rates are 15% on gross royalties and 15% on interest, but many comprehensive agreements provide 0% on arm’s length interest paid to a financial institution or pension fund, and 10% on royalties for industrial, scientific, or literary property. A royalty for the use of fitness-related software or patents may also qualify for a full 0% exemption if paid to a US resident under the Income Tax Convention Article XII (software royalties). The claim is activated by the same NR301 and residency proof procedure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CA$1,000,000 in aggregate annual value of controlled transactions involving inventory goods; CA$500,000 for controlled transactions involving services rental royalties and interest paid to non-residents; CA$100,000 for dividends? – Actually, the operative CRA-administered threshold is CA$1,000,000 for goods and CA$500,000 for services/intangibles/interest per taxpayer fiscal year. A separate CA$100,000 threshold applies to amounts of loans or advances made by a non-resident to the Canadian entity for which a T106 report must be filed whenever the total loans exceed that amount.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not enforce standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but the federal Income Tax Act contains robust anti-avoidance rules (general anti-avoidance rule – GAAR), OECD PCA pillar legislation labelled the ‘anti-hybrid mismatch rules’, and substance over form jurisprudence. Quebec’s Tax Act likewise imposes a civil `abuse of law` doctrine taxing transactions lacking a genuine commercial or economic substance. For a health-fitness app holding entity: retain local development IP, real office/cloud assets, and Quebec employees involved in decision-making. Shell status will trigger GAAR, reassessments, and 100% penalty under subsection 162(1).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Willful omission or misrepresentation of Canadian-source revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a T2 or CO-17 declaring no or lower Quebec/federal revenue while the user base and IAP income include Canadian residents; using offshore nominee payment processors to route Apple/Google app-store proceeds off-book.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under the Income Tax Act section 239 and Excise Tax Act: fine up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years (summary conviction up to 2 years). Quebec under Taxation Act section 81: civil penalties of 50%-150% of the additional tax payable plus daily interest. CRA can also impose a 10% gross-negligence penalty under subsection 163(2).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for corporate source deductions (CRA deemed trust), unpaid QST/GST, and any withheld taxes. Courts may pierce the corporate veil where the corporation is a sham or a “frustrated middleman”; personal orders for restitution, asset-freezing orders under the Income Tax Act, and travel bans are obtainable when a director flees the jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a dormant Quebec shelf corporation with no employees, no office, no real board activity, and routing subscription royalty revenue to a zero-tax Cayman associate, with no actual product development or risk function performed in Canada.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment disallowing transactions, plus a 5% mispricing penalty under subsection 247(3) where transfer pricing documentation is absent. Canada treats the shell as resident and assesses on worldwide income. Quebec may additionally apply the abuse doctrine and impose a penalty of up to 100% of the under-withheld amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director liability under the CCQ (Civil Code of Quebec) for fraud or a “masking” act; a court can disregard the corporate veil under the veil-piercing doctrine, making directors liable for all tax deficiencies plus punitive damages. Biometric data misuse during a shell operation also activates medical-health regulatory penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting app-store payments and wallet top-ups without maintaining customer due diligence files, failing to identify beneficial owners of corporate subscription accounts, or transacting in virtual currency without reporting to FINTRAC if the threshold of CA$10,000/day is exceed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act: up to CA$500,000 for a first offence per day for failing to register, failing to report, or non-identity verification. Criminal sanctions include imprisonment up to 5 years. Quebec-specific: AMF may revoke the digital-media tax credit if the entity has unpaid AML fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for design and enforcement failures; criminal fines enforced against the director’s personal assets, and prohibition orders block them from managing any Canadian entity for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging a Cayman or US parent a artificially high licence fee for the app software code; filing no Form T106 Transfer Pricing Report for a controlled transaction exceeding CAD 500,000; no contemporaneous local file or master file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA adjusts intercompany remuneration to arm’s-length and levies a penalty of 10% of the net under-assessed transfer price unless reasonable documentation was prepared and filed within 90 days of request. Additional assessment of 25% withholding on the deemed dividend if the price adjustment is treated as a shareholder benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the false price-setting arrangement may be assessed personally for the 10% gross-negligence penalty under subsection 247(3) where the veil is pierced for conspiracy to evade income tax; in egregious fraud, directors face criminal jail terms, travel bans, and confiscation of proceeds of the unhealthy tax-planning scheme.
